In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements.

**Statements:**

All pens are books.

All books are novels.

All novels are good.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some novels are pens.

II. All books are good.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.

questions.solution:
**Explanation:**

We draw a Venn diagram using the given statements:

All pens are books.

All books are novels.

All novels are good.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/179b657fad81358af590078a6287337bd84bfb8d2e26862a9902310d7260bf0a.png] 

Now we consider the given conclusions:

**I. Some novels are pens ****→ Follows** → Since 'all pens are books' and 'all books are pens' we can say that all pens are novels which can also be referred as some novels are pens and therefore the conclusion follows.

**II. All books are good ****→ Follows** → We have 'all books are novels' and 'all novels are good' so there is an indirect relation between books and good and it is safe to say that all books are good thus the conclusion follows.

So both conclusions I and II follows.

**Hence the correct answer is option 1.**

• It is formed by the union of the Kali and Trisuli rivers, which rise in the Great Himalaya Range in Nepal; from this junction to the Indian border the river is called the Narayani.
 
• It flows southwest into India and then turns southeast along with the Uttar Pradesh–Bihar state border and across the Indo-Gangetic Plain.
 
• It enters the Ganges (Ganga) River opposite Patna after a winding course of 475 miles (765 km).
 
• The Burhi (“Old”) Gandak flows parallel to and east of the Gandak River in an old channel.
 
• It joins the Ganges northeast of Munger.

• From its source, it flows north into the southeastern Rajasthan state. 
 
• Turning northeast, it flows past Kota and along the Rajasthan–Madhya Pradesh border; shifting east-southeast, it forms a portion of the **Uttar Pradesh-Madhya Pradesh border** and flows through Uttar Pradesh to empty into the Yamuna after a 550-mile (900-km) course.

• Also known as Vridha Ganga.
 
• Major left-bank tributaries: Purna, Pranhita, Indravati, and Sabari rivers.
 
• Major right bank tributaries: Pravara, Manjira, and Manair rivers.
 
• The Pranhita river is the largest tributary of Godavari.
 
• Important dams built across the Godavari river: Jayakwadi dam, Gangapur Dam, Babli project, and Sriram Sagar Dam.

questions.question: Bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances. This process is called as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**catabolism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances. This process is called as catabolism.
 
• The word **catabolism is from New Latin**, which got the roots from Greek: **κάτω Kato, "downward"** and** βάλλειν ballein**, "to throw".
 
• It breaks down large molecules like **polysaccharides, lipids, etc. into smaller units like monosaccharides, fatty acids, nucleotides, etc**.
 
• It is the breaking-down aspect of **metabolism**.
 
• Cells use the monomers released from breaking down polymers to either construct new polymer molecules or degrade them into simple waste products like **lactic acid, carbon dioxide, acetic acid, urea, and ammonia, releasing energy**.
 
• The creation of these wastes is usually an oxidation process involving a release of chemical-free energy. Of this, some are lost as heat, and the rest results in the formation of adenosine triphosphate (ATP).​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Catabolism** is a metabolic process in which complex molecules are broken down into simpler ones with the release of energy. In the context of the given statement, bacterial and fungal enzymes break down the complex detritus into simpler inorganic substances such as carbon dioxide, water, and mineral ions. This breakdown process releases energy that can be used by the decomposers or other organisms in the ecosystem.
 
• Fragmentation: Detritivores (e.g., earthworms) break down detritus into smaller particles. This process is called fragmentation.
 
• Leaching: By the process of leaching, water-soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts.
 
• Decomposition: It** **is the process of breaking down a substance into its constituent parts. Decomposition of dead organic matter occurs in nature and it is also called decay or putrefaction.​

• **Valency and molecular weight** are two related terms.
 
• The** quantity of electrons **in an** element's outermost shell **determines its valency.
 
• **Valence electrons **are the electrons that make up the** outermost shell surrounding an atomic nucleus.**
 
• The **nucleus **of an atom is composed of **protons and neutrons. **
 
• **Electrons **revolve around the nucleus in a fixed path called **orbits or shells.**
 
• The names of the shells are** "K," "L," "M," "N," **and so forth.
 
• The **'K' shel**l, which may hold up to **2 electrons**, is the innermost shell.
 
• The **"L" shell**, which has up to **8 electrons**, comes next.
 
• The** "M" shell, **which has up to **18 electrons**, comes next.
 
• Up to** 32 electrons** can be found in the last **"N" shell.**​
 
• **Boron:**
 
 
• The atomic number of boron is **5.**
 
• There are** fewer than five electrons—three**—in the outer shell.
 
• It needs to provide or release these **electrons to stay stable.**
 
• **Two electrons **are located in the** K shell **and three are located in the** L shell **in accordance with the** octet rule.**
 
• It'll lose **three electrons.**
 
• The result is that boron has a **valency of 3.**​

questions.question: A boat can travel 104 km downstream in 8 hours. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/h, then find in what time will it be able to cover 13 km upstream?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Downstream speed = 104 ÷ 8 = 13 km/h.

Upstream speed = Downstream speed − (2 × Speed of stream)

Upstream speed = 13 − (2 × 2) = 9 km/h.

Time for 13 km upstream = 13 ÷ 9 = 1 4/9 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 4/9 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Downstream distance = 104 km

Downstream time = 8 hours

Speed of stream (v) = 2 km/h

Upstream distance = 13 km

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Downstream speed (D) = u + v

Upstream speed (U) = u − v

Where u = speed of boat in still water and v = speed of stream.

 
• 
 

 Downstream: 104 km / 8 hrs = 13 km/h
 
• 
 

 Upstream: Distance = 13 km
 Result: Time = 13 ÷ 9 = 1 4/9 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream speed (D) = 104 ÷ 8 = 13 km/h

⇒ u + v = 13

⇒ u + 2 = 13

⇒ u = 13 − 2 = 11 km/h

⇒ Upstream speed (U) = u − v = 11 − 2 = 9 km/h

⇒ Time taken = Distance ÷ Upstream speed

⇒ Time taken = 13 ÷ 9 = 1 4/9 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 1 4/9 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speed

Downstream speed (D) = Speed of boat in still water (u) + Speed of stream (v). Upstream speed (U) = u − v.

Speed of Boat in Still Water

The speed of the boat in still water can be calculated as u = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of the Stream

questions.question: The number of factors of 196 which are divisible by 4 is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Prime factorization of **196** = 2² × 7².

To be divisible by **4** (2²), the factor must contain 2² as a component.

Factors divisible by 4 = (Number of ways to choose 2²) × (Number of ways to choose powers of 7).

Factors = 1 × (2 + 1) = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Reluctant
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Hesitant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The word 'reluctant' is 'unwilling and hesitant; disinclined'.
 
• Let's consider each option-
 
 
• Definite- Having certain or distinct limits
 
• Hesitant- **Tentative, unsure**, or slow in acting or speaking.
 
• Confident- Feeling or showing confidence in oneself or one's abilities or qualities.
 
• Indiscreet- Having, showing, or proceeding from too great a readiness to reveal things that should remain private or secret.
 
 
 
• Hence, the most appropriate synonym of the word 'reluctant' is 'hesitant'.
 
• Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.
